one-check-per-line.why: all 5 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 5

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: expect line 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 not quoted word for word in the builder brief: "Running `node src/app.js <tmp>/c.json`, where c.json contains the four lines `{`"

words-only.why: I compared each verifier check's PASS/FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Check 1 requires only "exit code is 1 and stdout ... is empty". Check 2 requires `bad config:`, the exact "$d/c.json" as passed, and line 3 and column 3 "in any readable form", which adds no wording rule. Check 3 passes when it prints `OK` and fails if the call returns or the message lacks the path. Check 4 matches its expect line: `listening on 9000`, exit 0 and `{"port":9000}`. Check 5 requires `npm test` to pass at head and at least one test that checks the path to fail against base src/, which is what the expect line says. The stricter items are all under "Advisory (not pass/fail conditions)": whether line and column depend on Node's message, ENOENT handling, returning {}, `cause`, and the README. No PASS or FAIL condition goes beyond what its expect line's words require.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs against the repository. Every file they name exists: `src/app.js`, `src/config.js`, `test/config.test.js` and README. `npm test` maps to `node --test`. The verifier's shell lines are valid as written: `d=$(mktemp -d); printf '{\n  "port": 9000,...' > $d/c.json`, `wc -c < $d/out` and `grep -F "$d/c.json" $d/err`. The `node --input-type=module -e "import {loadConfig} from './src/config.js'; ..."` snippets are valid ESM, and `$d` expands correctly inside the double quotes. `git checkout <base> -- src` and `git checkout HEAD -- src` are valid git. The `<base>` placeholder comes with ways to find it: `git merge-base HEAD origin/HEAD` or the PR's base SHA. The builder's steps either describe actions or reuse these same commands. I found no invalid syntax, no missing files and no wrong program arguments.

catches-traps.why: I checked both must_catch items against the builder brief. Item 1 is met. Step 1 says "Never return `{}`, defaults or any other value for malformed JSON." The out-of-scope line also lists "swallowing errors or returning defaults." Item 2 is met as well. The "Current code" section names `test/config.test.js` and says one of its tests "checks that `{port: 9000` throws `SyntaxError`." Step 1 then says "a SyntaxError is preferred, so the existing `assert.throws(..., SyntaxError)` test still passes." The brief never says outright that wrapping the error would break that test. It does point out that the existing test asserts SyntaxError, and it tells the builder to keep throwing a SyntaxError so the test still passes. That covers the trap.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked both briefs against the two must_not items, and neither brief does either one. Item 1: the builder brief does have the builder wrap `JSON.parse` in try/catch. But on a parse error it says to "throw a new error" with the path and location in it. It also says outright: "Never return `{}`, defaults or any other value for malformed JSON." So the builder is told to rethrow, not to catch and return a value. Item 2: verifier Check 2 accepts line 3 and column 3 "in any readable form (for example `line 3 column 3`, `3:3`, or `line 3, col 3`)". It fails a run only when something is missing or the numbers are not 3. It never fails a run just because the wording or order differs from one exact format. Nothing else in either brief falls under the must_not list.

methods-private.why: The criterion holds. I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief's checks. The builder brief has none of the verifier's specific probes: no `wc -c < $d/out`, no `grep -F 'bad config:'` or `grep -F "$d/c.json"`, and no inline `node --input-type=module -e "...includes(...) ? 'OK' : 'NO PATH'"` script. It also has no PASS/FAIL wording. Step 3 does run `node src/app.js $d/c.json` and states exit 1, empty stdout, the path, and line 3 / column 3. But that only restates expect lines 1–2, which is the bar, using a command the expect line names. Step 6 ("put the original `src/config.js` back temporarily, run `npm test`") is the issue's own proof 5, so it is an allowed command. The rest tells the builder to run `npm test` and write its own tests, which the criterion also allows.
